subject: NA value in the covariates for calculateDiffMeth

messages.author: 8fad3182e4b25354
messages.subject: NA value in the covariates for calculateDiffMeth
parts:
Greetings! 

I have several covariates that I would like to be accounted for when calculating the differentially methylated regions with calculateDiffMeth. One such covariate happens to have a missing value that R codes as NA.  When attempting to add this covariate into the calculateDiffMeth function I get this error message: 

Error in lm.fit(x, y, offset = offset, singlar.ok = singular.ok, ...) : 
0 (non-NA) cases 
In addition: Warning messages: 
1: In mclapply(cntlist, logReg, formula, vars, treatment = treatment, : 
all scheduled cores encountered errors in user code 
2: In is.na(x) : is.na() applied to non-(list or vector) of type NULL 

I tried several different ways of working around the NA including na.omit, na.exclude, na.action = na.exclude. None of which work. 

Is there a way to get calculateDiffMeth to ignore this NA value? 

Many thanks, 

Laetitia

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] NA value in the covariates for calculateDiffMeth
parts: you can ignore/drop the samples that have NA covariate value or try to impute the covariate values (don't know how in your specific case). The covariates are the same for all samples, and provided once to the function, you simply drop the samples in methylBase object whose covariates are NA. You can try to use reorganize() function to drop samples
